avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements (high-dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Chelation of zoledronic acid in GI tract reduces absorption and efficacy; high doses impair bisphosphonate bioavailability
avoid_supplements.action: Separate administration by minimum 2 hours; use lowest effective calcium dose; consider dietary sources instead

avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Iron chelates bisphosphonates, reducing drug absorption and therapeutic effect
avoid_supplements.action: Administer iron supplements at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after zoledronic acid IV infusion

avoid_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Magnesium binds bisphosphonates, significantly reducing systemic absorption
avoid_supplements.action: Separate dosing by minimum 2 hours; monitor for reduced therapeutic response

avoid_supplements.name: Aluminum-containing antacids
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; use alternative antacids (H2-blockers preferred)

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: While beneficial, excessive vitamin D with bisphosphonates may increase hypocalcemia risk in susceptible patients
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum calcium and vitamin D levels; coordinate supplementation with prescriber

caution_supplements.name: NSAIDs (as supplements/OTC)
caution_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs may increase GI upset and renal function stress when combined with bisphosphonates
caution_supplements.action: Use lowest effective dose; monitor renal function; consider gastroprotection if concurrent use necessary

avoid_foods.name: High-calcium foods consumed immediately before/after IV infusion
avoid_foods.mechanism: While zoledronic acid is IV-administered, concurrent high-calcium intake may alter serum calcium balance during drug redistribution phase
avoid_foods.action: Time high-calcium meals away from infusion day; maintain normal dietary calcium intake

caution_foods.name: Dairy products (milk, cheese, yogurt)
caution_foods.mechanism: High calcium content may theoretically affect mineral metabolism balance; not a direct drug interaction but worth monitoring
caution_foods.action: Maintain normal dietary dairy intake; ensure adequate but not excessive calcium from food sources

caution_foods.name: Foods high in oxalates (spinach, rhubarb, nuts)
caution_foods.mechanism: May chelate minerals and affect overall bone metabolism homeostasis during bisphosphonate therapy
caution_foods.action: No specific restriction needed; maintain balanced, varied diet

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum calcium, phosphate, magnesium, and renal function (eGFR) regularly, especially within 2 weeks post-infusion and annually. Assess for osteonecrosis of the jaw risk factors and atypical fractures; counsel patients on adequate calcium and vitamin D intake separate from drug administration timing.
